issues.title: Missing private modifier on gleanWrapper
issues.description: The rule requires that properties have explicit access control modifiers with 'private' for implementation details. The gleanWrapper property lacks the 'private' modifier, exposing an internal implementation detail that should not be accessible outside the struct.
issues.rule_name: Properties and Methods Must Have Appropriate Access Control

issues.title: Incorrect Reader Mode URL handling in cancelEditMode
issues.description: The cancelEditMode function now incorrectly preserves reader mode URLs when canceling edit mode. The logic was changed from '&&' (AND) to '||' (OR), which means reader mode URLs will now be kept instead of being cleared. This breaks the expected behavior where reader mode URLs should be filtered out when canceling URL editing, potentially causing the address bar to display internal reader:// URLs to users instead of the original webpage URL.

issues.title: Inverted reader mode telemetry state tracking
issues.description: The recordReaderModeTelemetry function has inverted logic for determining reader mode state. When the reader mode is 'available' (about to be enabled), it reports false instead of true, and for all other states it reports true instead of false. This causes telemetry data to incorrectly track reader mode usage patterns - reporting that reader mode is being disabled when it's actually being enabled and vice versa. This will corrupt analytics data about reader mode feature usage.

issues.title: Wrong display view type for reader mode action
issues.description: The handleShowReaderModeAction function sets the wrong displayView type when the user taps the reader mode button. Instead of setting displayView to '.readerMode' (which would show the reader mode view), it's set to '.readerModeLongPressAction' (which is meant for long-press actions). This causes the wrong UI component to be displayed when users try to activate reader mode, breaking the core reader mode functionality and showing an incorrect action sheet instead of the reader view.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #31577 - Remove FXIOS-14593 [BVC] Clean up qr code related code from BVC

structured_output.summary:
This PR removes the QR code scanner entry points from the browser: the QRCodeViewControllerDelegate conformance on BrowserViewController, the `handleQRCode` coordinator path, the `qrCode` toolbar action and its telemetry, the `QRCode` quick action and deeplink route, and the `qr_code.scanned` and `toolbar.qr_scan_button_tapped` Glean metrics. The removal itself is mostly clean. Plist and Swift references to the QR shortcut and metrics are gone, and the matching tests were removed with the code.

The PR also contains changes that are not QR cleanup. The biggest is in `BrowserViewControllerState`, where `handleShowReaderModeAction` now maps to `.readerModeLongPressAction` instead of `.readerMode`. That sends the `showReaderMode` action, which the accessibility magic tap dispatches, into the add-to-Reading-List path. In `ToolbarMiddleware`, the telemetry for reader mode now has its boolean inverted, and `cancelEditMode` has a `&&` changed to `||`. A version bump to 147.2 is also included. None of these are explained by the title or description, and no tests cover them.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The QR removal itself is sound, but the PR also carries at least one user-facing regression (magic tap on reader mode now adds the page to the Reading List) and one telemetry inversion. Both are unrelated to the stated goal and untested. Those need fixing or splitting out before merge.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, the QR code scanner was reachable from several entry points: the address toolbar's `qrCode` button (ToolbarMiddleware), the Home Screen `QRCode` quick action (QuickActions → DeeplinkInput.ShortcutType → RouteBuilder → Route.AppAction `.showQRCode`), and BrowserViewController acting as a `QRCodeViewControllerDelegate`. Taps went through the Redux-style toolbar middleware, which dispatches `GeneralBrowserAction`s; `BrowserViewControllerState` reduces those into a `displayView` value; and `BrowserViewController.handleDisplayActions` switches on it to present UI. Telemetry is recorded via `ToolbarTelemetry` and `TelemetryWrapper` into Glean metrics.

This PR deletes the QR entry points from every one of those layers and the matching Glean probes. It also changes the reader-mode mapping in `BrowserViewControllerState` and the reader-mode telemetry and cancel-edit logic in `ToolbarMiddleware`. Those last changes sit in the same reducer and middleware, but they are not part of the QR path.
steps: Entry points: the toolbar `qrCode` button, the `QRCode` Home Screen quick action, and the `route-action` deeplink all end in a `showQRCode` or `showQRcodeReader` action. This PR removes all three, along with `QRCodeViewControllerDelegate` on BVC.

Routing: `Route.AppAction.showQRCode` and `RouteBuilder`'s `.qrCode` case are removed, so `BrowserCoordinator` no longer calls `browserViewController.handleQRCode()`. Shortcut and deeplink parsing no longer produce a QR route.

State: `BrowserViewControllerState` drops the `.qrCodeReader` display type and its reducer. In the same file, `handleShowReaderModeAction` now returns `.readerModeLongPressAction` instead of `.readerMode`, which changes where the `showReaderMode` action goes.

Middleware: `ToolbarMiddleware` drops the `.qrCode` button handler. It also changes `cancelEditMode` (`&&` becomes `||`) and inverts the `isEnabled` value in `recordReaderModeTelemetry`. These two changes are not related to QR.

Telemetry: `qr_code.scanned` and `toolbar.qr_scan_button_tapped` are removed from the Glean YAML and from `TelemetryWrapper` and `ToolbarTelemetry`. `ToolbarTelemetry.gleanWrapper` is also widened from private to internal with no caller that needs it.

findings.title: Magic-tap reader-mode action now adds the page to the Reading List
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Browser/BrowserViewController/State/BrowserViewControllerState.swift`, `handleShowReaderModeAction` (around line 566) was changed to set `displayView: .readerModeLongPressAction`. Revert it to `.readerMode`, which `BrowserViewController.handleDisplayActions` (around line 2872 in `BrowserViewController.swift`) maps to `toggleReaderMode()`. The `showReaderMode` action is dispatched by `accessibilityPerformMagicTap` (around line 2394) and must still toggle reader mode, not add the page to the Reading List. Keep the QR removal otherwise intact. Add a unit test in the BrowserViewControllerState tests asserting that `showReaderMode` yields `displayView == .readerMode`.

findings.title: Reader-mode telemetry records the enabled state inverted
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Browser/Toolbars/Redux/ToolbarMiddleware.swift`, `recordReaderModeTelemetry` (around lines 521-528) inverted the `isReaderModeEnabled` switch. Restore the original mapping: `.available` should yield `true` (the comment says the mode will be enabled after the action runs), and `default` should yield `false`. Keep the change limited to this switch. Also consider moving this change into a separate PR, since it is unrelated to QR cleanup. Add a middleware test that asserts `readerModeButtonTapped` is recorded with `isEnabled: true` when `readerModeState` is `.available`.

findings.title: Unrelated flip of && to || in cancelEditMode
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Browser/Toolbars/Redux/ToolbarMiddleware.swift`, `cancelEditMode` (around line 485) changed `isWebPage() && !isReaderModeURL` to `isWebPage() || isReaderModeURL`. This is unrelated to the QR removal. Restore the original `&&`/`!` expression unless there is a documented reason for the change. If the change is intended, split it into its own PR and add a test covering reader-mode URLs when cancelling edit mode.

findings.title: Unrelated app version bump to 147.2 in a cleanup PR
findings.body:
`version.xcconfig` changes `APP_VERSION` from 147.1 to 147.2. The PR title and description do not mention a release bump. Version bumps usually belong in a release-prep commit, not in a feature cleanup. If it was added by accident, it could ship a version number nobody intended.

::diff{file="firefox-ios/Client/Configuration/version.xcconfig" lines="1-1"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Configuration/version.xcconfig`, `APP_VERSION` was bumped from 147.1 to 147.2 in a PR that only removes QR code code. Confirm whether this bump is intended. If not, revert it to `APP_VERSION = 147.1`. If it is intended, move it to a release-prep PR so the version history stays clean.

findings.title: ToolbarTelemetry.gleanWrapper widened to internal without a caller
findings.body:
`ToolbarTelemetry.gleanWrapper` changed from `private` to internal. Nothing in this PR reads the property from outside the struct, and the tests inject the wrapper through `init`. Widening access just exposes an implementation detail. Revert it unless a caller needs it.

::diff{file="firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Browser/Toolbars/ToolbarTelemetry.swift" lines="6-12"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Browser/Toolbars/ToolbarTelemetry.swift`, `gleanWrapper` (line 9) was changed from `private let` to `let`. Restore `private let gleanWrapper: GleanWrapper`, since no code in the PR needs access outside the struct. Build the app and the ClientTests target to confirm nothing depends on the wider access.

findings.title: No tests cover the reader-mode mapping or telemetry changes
findings.body:
The PR deletes three QR-related tests and adds none. It changes the `showReaderMode` display mapping, the reader-mode telemetry `isEnabled` value, and `cancelEditMode`, and no test catches any of them. `ToolbarMiddlewareTests` already has a `didTapButton` harness that could cover the telemetry case. The `BrowserViewControllerState` reducer could be tested directly for the `showReaderMode` display type.

::code{file="firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/ClientTests/Toolbar/ToolbarMiddlewareTests.swift" lines="311-320"}
findings.fixPrompt: Add tests for the reader-mode behavior touched by this PR. In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/ClientTests/Toolbar/ToolbarMiddlewareTests.swift`, add a case asserting that `readerModeButtonTapped` is recorded with `isEnabled: true` when `readerModeState` is `.available`, and `false` otherwise. Follow the existing `didTapButton` tests in that file. Add a `BrowserViewControllerState` reducer test asserting that `GeneralBrowserActionType.showReaderMode` produces `displayView == .readerMode`. Also add a `cancelEditMode` test for a reader-mode URL.

findings.title: QR shortcut, route, and metric removal done cleanly
findings.body:
The QR code cleanup is thorough. Every removed symbol (`ShortcutType.qrCode`, `AppAction.showQRCode`, `GeneralBrowserActionType.showQRcodeReader`, `ToolbarActionType`'s `.qrCode`, the `qrCodeText`/`qrCodeURL` telemetry cases, `GleanMetrics.QrCode.scanned`, and `toolbar.qr_scan_button_tapped`) has no remaining references outside the generated project file. `Info.plist` never listed a QR quick action, so there is no dangling shortcut. The `QRCodeViewController` stack is still used by the settings and sync sign-in flows, so keeping it is the right call.

::code{file="firefox-ios/Client/Telemetry/TelemetryWrapper.swift" lines="824-830"}
